author: rod0352
body:
This PR ensures the dashboard automatically reflects status changes, eliminating the need for a manual refresh.

The Problem:
After a user performed a status-changing action (e.g., approving a study), the dashboard would navigate but show stale data until the page was manually refreshed.

Solution:
client-side cache invalidation strategy using tanstack-query (react-query).

1. From Server Components to Client-Side Queries: The dashboards, which were previously fetching data on the server, have been refactored. They now contain client-side components that use the useQuery hook to fetch and manage their own data.

2. Cache Invalidation on Mutation: The components that trigger status changes (e.g., the "Approve" and "Submit" buttons) now use queryClient.invalidateQueries in their onSuccess handlers.

The Flow:
   1. A user performs an action (e.g., approves a study).
   2. The mutation succeeds.
   3. The onSuccess callback invalidates the query key associated with the dashboard's data.
   4. The user is navigated to the dashboard via router.push.
   5. When the dashboard mounts, tanstack-query sees the invalidated query and automatically refetches the data, ensuring the user sees the latest status.

This PR pins [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) to the latest release **7.10.5**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.10.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Big speed improvements for ``coverage combine``: it's now about twice as
  fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests `2032 <pull 2032_>`_,
  `2033 <pull 2033_>`_, and `2034 <pull 2034_>`_.

.. _pull 2032: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2032
.. _pull 2033: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2033
.. _pull 2034: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2034


.. _changes_7-10-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added ``patch = fork`` for times when the built-in forking support is
  insufficient.

- Fix: ``patch = execv`` also inherits the entire coverage configuration now.


.. _changes_7-10-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fixes for ``patch = subprocess``:

  - If subprocesses spawned yet more subprocesses simultaneously, some coverage
    could be missed.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2024`_.

  - If subprocesses were created in other directories, their data files were
    stranded there and not combined into the totals, as described in `issue
    2025`_.  This is now fixed.

  - On Windows (or maybe only some Windows?) the patch would fail with a
    ``ModuleNotFound`` error trying to import coverage.  This is now fixed,
    closing `issue 2022`_.

  - Originally only options set in the coverage configuration file would apply
    to subprocesses.  Options set on the ``coverage run`` command line (such as
    ``--branch``) wouldn't be communicated to the subprocesses.  This could
    lead to combining failures, as described in `issue 2021`_. Now the entire
    configuration is used in subprocesses, regardless of its origin.

  - Added ``debug=patch`` to help diagnose problems.

- Fix: really close all SQLite databases, even in-memory ones. Closes `issue
  2017`_.

.. _issue 2017: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2017
.. _issue 2021: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2021
.. _issue 2022: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2022
.. _issue 2024: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2024
.. _issue 2025: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2025


.. _changes_7-10-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some code with NOP bytecodes could report missing branches that are
  actually executed. This is now fixed, closing `issue 1999`_. Python 3.9
  still shows the problem.

.. _issue 1999: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1999


.. _changes_7-10-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the exclusion for ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` was wrong: it marked the branch
  as partial, but it should have been a line exclusion so the entire clause
  would be excluded. Improves `issue 831`_.

- Fix: changed where .pth files are written for ``patch = subprocess``, closing
  `issue 2006`_.

.. _issue 2006: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2006


.. _changes_7-10-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_, its duplicate `issue 378`_ and old
    `issue 689`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes
  `issue 831`_.

- A new command-line option: ``--save-signal=USR1`` specifies a signal that
  coverage.py will listen for.  When the signal is sent, the coverage data will
  be saved.  This makes it possible to save data from within long-running
  processes.  Thanks, `Arkady Gilinsky <pull 1998_>`_.

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_report_partial_also`" is a list of
  regexes to add as pragmas for partial branches.  This parallels the
  ":ref:`config_report_exclude_also`" setting for adding line exclusion
  patterns.

- A few file path configuration settings didn't allow for tilde expansion:
  :ref:`config_json_output`, :ref:`config_lcov_output` and
  :ref:`config_run_debug_file`.  This is now fixed.

- Wheels are included for 3.14 now that 3.14 rc1 is available.

- We no longer ship a PyPy-specific wheel. PyPy will install the pure-Python
  wheel.  Closes `issue 2001`_.

- In the very unusual situation of not having a current frame, coverage no
  longer crashes when using the sysmon core, fixing `issue 2005`_.

.. _issue 310: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/310
.. _issue 312: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/312
.. _issue 367: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/367
.. _issue 378: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/378

This commit introduces a complete rewrite of the Bitchat application from Swift/SwiftUI to Rust with the egui framework.

The new version preserves the core functionality and protocol of the original application:
- Asynchronous, multi-threaded architecture using Tokio.
- BLE communication for discovering and connecting to peers using `btleplug`.
- End-to-end encryption using the Noise Protocol Framework (`XX` pattern) via the `snow` crate.
- A custom binary protocol for messages, implemented with `serde` and `bincode`.
- A responsive GUI built with `egui`, running in its own thread.

The application is structured into several modules:
- `main`: UI loop and application setup.
- `network`: A central `NetworkManager` that orchestrates all other components.
- `ble`: A task for handling low-level BLE operations.
- `noise`: A service for managing Noise Protocol sessions.
- `protocol`: Definitions for the core data structures.

This rewrite provides a cross-platform foundation for the Bitchat application.

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive enterprise-ready deployment solution for the OpenFGA operator using Kustomize, fulfilling the requirements for a fully deployable OpenFGA offering with all supporting services and enterprise-grade configurations.

## 🚀 Key Features Implemented

### Enterprise Infrastructure
- **Kustomize-based deployment architecture** with base configurations and environment-specific overlays
- **Production-ready OpenFGA operator** with high availability (3 replicas), security contexts, and comprehensive monitoring
- **Enterprise RBAC** with least-privilege access controls and comprehensive permissions

### Identity & Access Management
- **Keycloak integration** for enterprise SSO with support for SAML, OIDC, and Active Directory
- **Multi-tenancy support** with role-based access control and secure tenant isolation
- **Production clustering** with automated failover and session replication

### Persistent Storage
- **Portworx enterprise storage** with three optimized storage classes:
  - `portworx-sc-db`: High-performance database storage (3 replicas)
  - `portworx-sc-replicated`: General purpose replicated storage (2 replicas)  
  - `portworx-sc-single`: Development single replica storage
- **Automated backup policies** with configurable retention and disaster recovery
- **Volume snapshot management** for point-in-time recovery

### Security & Compliance
- **Comprehensive admission controllers** with both validating and mutating webhooks
- **Network security policies** implementing zero-trust architecture with default-deny rules
- **Security-first containers** with non-root users, read-only filesystems, and dropped capabilities
- **Pod Security Standards** enforcement with restricted security contexts

### Network Observability
- **Cilium Hubble integration** for advanced network flow monitoring and visualization
- **Hubble UI** providing web-based network observability dashboard
- **Real-time security insights** with network policy enforcement monitoring
- **Prometheus integration** for comprehensive metrics collection

## 📁 Project Structure

```
kustomize/
├── base/                          # Base configurations
│   ├── admission-controller/      # Validation & mutation webhooks
│   ├── crds/                     # Custom Resource Definitions
│   ├── keycloak/                 # Identity provider configuration
│   ├── network-observability/    # Cilium Hubble setup
│   ├── network-policies/         # Zero-trust network security
│   ├── operator/                 # OpenFGA operator deployment
│   └── storage/                  # Portworx storage configuration
└── overlays/                     # Environment-specific configs
    ├── dev/                      # Development (1 replica, debug logging)
    └── prod/                     # Production (3 replicas, audit logging)
```

## 🛠️ Enhanced Developer Experience

### Makefile Automation
Added comprehensive Makefile targets for streamlined operations:

```bash
make deploy-dev      # Deploy to development environment
make deploy-prod     # Deploy to production environment  
make check-kustomize # Validate all Kustomize configurations
make verify-deployment # Check deployment status
```

### Enterprise Example
Included production-ready OpenFGA instance example (`examples/enterprise-openfga.yaml`) demonstrating:
- OIDC authentication with Keycloak
- Portworx persistent storage
- Comprehensive security configurations
- Monitoring and observability integration

## 🔒 Security Enhancements

### Admission Control
- **Image signature verification** ensuring only approved container images
- **Security policy enforcement** with automatic security context injection
- **Resource validation** preventing misconfigurations

### Network Security
- **Microsegmentation** with namespace and pod-level network policies
- **Default-deny ingress/egress** with explicit allow rules for required communication
- **Service mesh integration** ready for advanced traffic management

## 📊 Enterprise Readiness

### High Availability
- **Multi-replica deployments** with pod anti-affinity rules
- **Automated failover** with leader election
- **Cross-zone distribution** for resilience

### Monitoring & Observability
- **Prometheus metrics** for all components
- **Structured logging** with correlation IDs
- **Distributed tracing** with OpenTelemetry integration
- **SLA monitoring** and alerting

### Compliance & Auditing
- **Comprehensive audit logging** for all operations
- **Security event tracking** with immutable log storage
- **Compliance framework support** (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST)

## 🌐 SaaS Integration Foundation

This implementation establishes the groundwork for SaaS offerings by providing:
- **Multi-tenant architecture** with secure isolation
- **Scalable infrastructure** supporting multiple customer deployments
- **Automated provisioning** through Kustomize overlays
- **Enterprise security** meeting compliance requirements

## 📚 Documentation

Comprehensive documentation includes:
- **Deployment guides** with step-by-step instructions
- **Architecture overview** explaining all components
- **Troubleshooting guides** with common issues and solutions
- **Customization examples** for different environments

## ✅ Validation

All configurations have been thoroughly tested:
- **Kustomize validation** passes for all environments
- **Security policy compliance** verified
- **Resource definitions** validated against Kubernetes schemas
- **Integration testing** completed successfully

This PR transforms the OpenFGA operator from a basic deployment into a comprehensive enterprise-grade authorization platform, ready for production use and SaaS integration.

author: cvazquezbr
body:
This commit fixes a critical bug that caused a crash when saving an edited image.

The `regenerateSingleImage` function was attempting to use the `HTMLCanvasElement` returned by the `composeImage` utility as an image `src` URL. This is incorrect and was causing an unhandled error: "Failed to load composed background for regeneration."

The fix modifies `regenerateSingleImage` to correctly handle the returned canvas object. Instead of trying to load it as a new image, the code now directly uses `ctx.drawImage()` to draw the composed background canvas onto the final canvas. This resolves the crash and makes the image regeneration process robust.

author: copilot
body:
This PR completely refactors the IceCubesApp networking layer from URLSession to Alamofire while maintaining 100% API compatibility with the existing codebase.

## Overview

The networking layer consisted of 5 separate clients that all used URLSession directly for HTTP requests. This refactoring modernizes the networking stack by adopting Alamofire, a mature and feature-rich networking library that provides better error handling, cleaner syntax, and improved maintainability.

## Changes Made

### Core Networking Client (`Client.swift`)
- Replaced `URLSession` with Alamofire `Session`
- Updated all HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) to use `AF.request()`
- Implemented multipart uploads using `AF.upload()` with proper form data handling
- Preserved WebSocket functionality using URLSession (Alamofire doesn't support WebSockets)
- Maintained OAuth token management and authorization headers
- Enhanced error handling while preserving custom `ServerError` decoding

### Specialized Clients
- **DeepLClient**: Translation service now uses Alamofire with form-encoded parameters
- **OpenAIClient**: AI features with custom `RawDataEncoding` for JSON payloads
- **SubClubClient**: Premium features with simplified error handling
- **InstanceSocialClient**: Instance discovery with preserved custom sorting logic

### Package Dependencies
- Added Alamofire 5.8.0+ as a dependency to the Network package
- Updated Package.swift to include Alamofire in target dependencies

### Testing & Validation
- Updated NetworkTests with comprehensive initialization and authentication tests
- Verified all public APIs remain unchanged
- Confirmed async/await patterns and thread safety are preserved

## Technical Details

### API Compatibility
All public method signatures remain exactly the same, ensuring zero breaking changes:
```swift
// These methods work identically to before
let account: Account = try await client.get(endpoint: Accounts.account(id: "123"))
let response = try await client.post(endpoint: Statuses.post(json: statusData))
let upload = try await client.mediaUpload(endpoint: Media.upload, ...)
```

### Error Handling
The existing error handling patterns are preserved, including custom `ServerError` decoding and HTTP status code handling. Alamofire's enhanced error reporting provides additional context while maintaining compatibility.

### WebSocket Support
Since Alamofire doesn't support WebSockets, the `makeWebSocketTask` method continues to use URLSession. This is isolated and documented, ensuring streaming functionality remains intact.

### Thread Safety
The existing `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` pattern for thread-safe state management is preserved, maintaining the same concurrency guarantees.

## Benefits

- **Modern Architecture**: Industry-standard networking with Alamofire
- **Better Error Handling**: More robust error handling and response validation
- **Cleaner Code**: Reduced boilerplate and improved readability
- **Enhanced Maintainability**: Easier to extend and modify networking logic
- **Future-Ready**: Built-in support for advanced features like request interceptors and retry logic

## Testing

The refactoring has been validated through:
- Compilation verification of all networking clients
- Updated unit tests covering initialization and authentication flows
- Verification that all existing app code continues to work without changes
- Confirmation that WebSocket streaming functionality is preserved

This change sets up the networking layer for future enhancements while maintaining complete backward compatibility with the existing codebase.

author: rylan12
body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/20553

This PR moves the `PathnameWriteMkpath` refinement out of `Formulary` into its own `WriteMkpathExtension` under `extend/pathname`. To avoid monkey patching globally, this is only prepended onto `Pathname` within the `build.rb` script, since the monkey patch will be scoped to the isolated build process.

There was a mention in https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/11307,  of deprecating this extension, which we could also do now. I think this would mean adding a `safe_write` method to `Pathname` everywhere in Homebrew, and then deprecating any uses of `WriteMkpathExtension#write` that require special handling in favor of `safe_write`. This could probably be done easily with a new RuboCop check as well.
